claims.text: The initial almost-equiatomic FeCoNi-based alloy has an fcc structure.
The initial FeCoNi-based alloy has high saturation magnetization.
The initial FeCoNi-based alloy exhibits soft ferromagnetism and low coercivity.
A controlled fraction of the alloying elements can be replaced by W while retaining an almost-equiatomic high-entropy composition.
The proposed alloy must have configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
Controlled processing such as rapid solidification or heat treatment can preserve a single-phase fcc structure and avoid phase separation in the W-modified alloy.
W incorporation induces local lattice distortions and strain fields because of its size and electronic differences from the other transition metals.
W incorporation enhances spin–orbit coupling in the alloy.
W-induced lattice strain and enhanced spin–orbit coupling increase magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Increased magnetocrystalline anisotropy promotes stronger pinning of magnetic domains.
Stronger magnetic-domain pinning produces higher coercivity.
The W-modified alloy will have significantly greater coercivity than FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt baseline alloys.
The W-modified alloy will maintain high saturation magnetization.
The W-modified alloy will maintain an almost-equiatomic, single-phase fcc structure.
Previously studied FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt alloys exhibit soft ferromagnetism and low coercivity.
Excessive W addition or inappropriate processing may cause secondary-phase formation and invalidate the expected coercivity enhancement.
